title: Rigour: checkable, honest, integrity-safe
summary: Get answers you can check, and use AI in ways your university will accept.

lessons.title: Mitigating Confabulation & Enforcing Epistemic Humility
lessons.body:
Language models do not possess a ground-truth database; they generate tokens based on statistical plausibility. Consequently, when asked for citations, statistics, or niche facts, models frequently **confabulate** (hallucinate plausible-sounding author names, journal titles, DOIs, and page numbers).

**Engineering Checkable Prompt Patterns:**
* **Uncertainty Calibration**: Instruct the model: *'If you are not 100% confident based on established peer-reviewed consensus, explicitly state "Unverified" rather than guessing.'*
* **Verification Mandates**: Ask the model to quote direct passages from supplied text rather than summarizing from memory.
* **External Verification Rule**: Always treat model citations as search queries to verify independently in your university library catalogue or PubMed/Google Scholar—never paste unverified citations into assessed coursework.

lessons.title: Academic Integrity & Ethical Co-Piloting
lessons.body:
UK universities (under QAA and Russell Group guidance) distinguish between **legitimate generative AI co-piloting** and **academic misconduct (plagiarism / contract cheating)**.

* **Legitimate Pedagogical Use**: Using AI as a Socratic sparring partner, brainstorming counter-arguments to your thesis, checking paragraph transition flow, generating practice exam questions, and debugging software code.
* **Prohibited Misconduct**: Prompting an AI to write your essay, generating sections of assessed text, or submitting AI-synthesized prose as your own work.
* **Best Practice**: Keep an audit trail of your research notes and prompts. If required by your department, declare your AI usage transparently (specifying the model, the date, and how the tool was applied).

exercises.title: Ask for verifiable help
exercises.scenario: You need background on a topic and must cite real sources.
exercises.task: Write a prompt that asks for checkable claims and honest uncertainty.

checks.label: Asks to flag uncertainty
checks.hint: Ask it to say when it is unsure.

checks.label: Warns against invention
checks.hint: Tell it not to invent references.

exercises.model_answer_tip: 'Give me background on X. Cite real sources I can look up, say if you are unsure, and do not invent any references.'

exercises.title: Feedback, not ghost-writing
exercises.scenario: You wrote an essay draft and want help improving it without the AI writing it.
exercises.task: Ask for feedback on YOUR draft, not a rewrite.

checks.label: Refuses a rewrite
checks.hint: Say it must not rewrite or write for you.

checks.label: Refers to your own draft
checks.hint: Say it is your own work.

exercises.model_answer_tip: 'Here is my own draft. Give feedback against the marking criteria below. Do not rewrite any sentences; point to weaknesses and suggest what to improve.'

exercises.title: Declare your AI use
exercises.scenario: Your module requires an AI-use declaration.
exercises.task: Ask for help drafting an honest declaration of how you used AI.

checks.label: Asks to list what the AI did
checks.hint: Say you will list what the AI did.

checks.label: Keeps it truthful
checks.hint: Ask it to stay accurate to what you actually did.

exercises.model_answer_tip: 'Help me write a short, honest AI-use declaration. I used it only to explain concepts and check grammar. List exactly that and nothing more.'
